newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian Queen lays stone for airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian Queen lays stone for airport terminal.

text.p: Cambodia's Queen Norodom Monineath on Friday laid the foundation stone of a new international passenger terminal to boost capacity at the capital's Pochentong Airport.

The terminal, designed by French architects, will be able to handle 1.2 million passengers a year when the first phase of work is completed in 1999, Transport and Public Works Minister Ing Kieth said.
The design leaves room for capacity to be boosted to two million passengers a year, said officials of the French-Malaysian consortium Societe Concessionaire de l'Aeroport (SCA).
SCA is renovating and managing the airport at a cost of about $100 million, including a grant from the French government and a $38 million loan from Malaysian and French banks.
Pochentong is expected this year to handle about one million passengers at its current terminal, which was upgraded and renovated last year. The new terminal will handle all international flights.
SCA includes France's GTM-Entrepose group and the joint venture Malaysian-Cambodian firm Muhibbah Masteron Cambodia.
